model: LQ design problem J(c; x_T) = 2<c, x_T>_w - ||c||^2_w on a reversible environment; blind c=0, stale c=x_S, damped c=P_tau x_S, oracle c=x_T. Payoffs evaluated on simulated states; the premium formulas are never fed into the payoff computation.

harnesses.A: exact-transition multi-mode OU (no time discretisation); tau_c_sim.py -> tau_c_results.json
harnesses.A_prime: common-random-number crossing root-find + block bootstrap; tau_c_sim.py
harnesses.B: AR(1) estimation of lambda from finite series; tau_c_sim.py
harnesses.C: forward Wright-Fisher with symmetric mutation (bounded, non-Gaussian, discrete population); tau_c_sim.py + refine.py -> refine_results.json
harnesses.D: Wright-Fisher SPLIT (two sister populations from a stationary ancestor); split_sim.py -> split_results.json

positive_controls.tau_0: PASS. stale = damped = oracle = 0.99917 +/- 0.00100, blind = 0, V = 1.
positive_controls.tau_infinity: damped -> 5.4e-12 (= blind) PASS. stale -> -1.0024 +/- 0.0017 (= -V, NOT blind). oracle -> +1.0001 +/- 0.0010 (= +V, NOT blind). The stated control 'all three converge to blind' is WRONG for stale and oracle; if stale converged to blind the sign-flip claim would be false.

verdicts.1_horizon_optimal_is_P_tau_g: SUPPORTED (damped attains the max of the measured value over the alpha sweep at alpha = rho, all horizons).
verdicts.2_damped_premium_exp_neg_2_lam_tau_V: CONFIRMED. |z| <= 2.3 over 22 horizons; positive at every horizon tested out to lam*tau = 7.
verdicts.3_stale_premium_2exp_neg_lam_tau_minus_1: CONFIRMED. |z| <= 2.7 over 22 horizons; strictly negative past tau_c.
verdicts.4_sign_flip_at_tau_c: CONFIRMED. Measured crossing 0.69411, bootstrap CI95 [0.69289, 0.69524], M = 8e6; log 2 = 0.693147 lies inside.
verdicts.d_multi_rate: CONFIRMED and MATERIAL. The mixture equation E[2 exp(-lam tau_c)] = 1 is right in all three configurations; log2/lam_slowest overstates tau_c by 71% to 715%.
verdicts.damping_never_hurts: TRUE ONLY FOR alpha < 2 rho. Measured premium of shrinkage alpha is alpha(2 rho - alpha) V (32/32 cells, |z| < 1.3). Damping with the CORRECT factor never hurts; damping with alpha > 2 rho does hurt.

finding_1_lambda_belongs_to_the_signal_n.process: Wright-Fisher, N=500, u=0.005 (theta=4Nu=10), 5920 chains, T=1492 gens
finding_1_lambda_belongs_to_the_signal_n.reading: Same environment, two value signals, tau_c differing by 2.1x; the plausible process-level guess is off by 10-21x.

finding_2_tau_is_path_length_not_diverge.model: stationary ancestor splits; two descendants evolve independently for d generations
finding_2_tau_is_path_length_not_diverge.reading: tau is the total path length between source and target, = 2 x divergence depth. Reading tau off the split time halves tau and doubles the apparent tau_c.

finding_3_estimating_lambda_from_data.method: AR(1) regression on a finite series of the environment, lam_true = 1, dt = 0.1
finding_3_estimating_lambda_from_data.reading: tau_c inherits the full sampling error of lam and is biased high at small n. At 50 observations the 95% interval for tau_c spans a factor of 12.7.

finding_4_shrinkage_is_robust_where_tau_.law: premium of shrinkage alpha over blind = alpha(2 rho - alpha) V, measured over 32 (tau, alpha) cells, |z| < 1.3
finding_4_shrinkage_is_robust_where_tau_.safe_region: 0 < alpha < 2 rho, equivalently lam_hat > lam - log2/tau
finding_4_shrinkage_is_robust_where_tau_.reading: OVER-estimating lambda is always safe (any alpha in (0, rho) strictly beats blind). UNDER-estimating is safe only within log2/tau. So the shrinkage rule tolerates a mis-identified lambda far better than the tau_c threshold does; the threshold is the fragile part of the result, the rule is not.

finding_5_a_real_stale_design_is_noisy.model: c = alpha (x_S + eps), eps ~ N(0, s2) independent of the environment
finding_5_a_real_stale_design_is_noisy.law: premium = 2 alpha rho V - alpha^2 (V + s2); crossing at rho = alpha (1 + s2/V)/2
finding_5_a_real_stale_design_is_noisy.reading: Fitting noise moves tau_c EARLIER, never later: log2/lam is an UPPER bound on the real crossover. A design with s2 >= V never beats blind at any horizon. Existing shrinkage (alpha<1) pushes it later. log2/lam is exact only for a noiselessly-estimated, unshrunk design.

residual_tensions.wf_theta_0.6_linear: measured 470.81, CI95 [464.23, 477.55] vs exact 461.75 -- +2.0%, about 2.5 sigma high. The lowest-theta (most U-shaped, heaviest-tailed) configuration. The two higher-precision configurations agree to 0.3% and 0.1%, so this is read as Monte Carlo, not a defect in the law.
not_tested: non-reversible couplings (every claim rests on reversibility; nothing here probes what breaks without it)
